category_title: Socially isolated boys who bully to gain friends and show off
student_description: This student is profoundly lonely and socially isolated, using bullying as a misguided attempt to gain friends while suppressing his own anger and frustration. Because he trusts no one but himself and refuses to discuss his own feelings directly, he uniquely requires emotionally safe, distanced interventions—such as role-play and third-person projection—to explore his emotions without feeling vulnerable.

criteria.rationale: Because the student suppresses his own emotions and trusts only himself, he needs the safety of discussing a fictional character's feelings rather than his own.
criteria.check: The tutor frames questions or reflections about emotions through the lens of a character, role-play scenario, or hypothetical third party, rather than asking the student directly about his own feelings.

criteria.rationale: Explicitly signaling when a role-play begins or ends (akin to using a physical prop) maintains the emotional safety boundary the student requires to open up.
criteria.check: The tutor explicitly establishes, maintains, or signals transitions in and out of a role-play or hypothetical scenario (e.g., using phrases like 'Let's pretend', 'Speaking as the character', or 'Stepping out of the story').

criteria.rationale: The student's bullying stems from profound loneliness, so exploring the emotional 'why' is more effective than focusing on the physical 'what' of the bullying incident.
criteria.check: The tutor directs the conversation toward the internal feelings, social motivations, or verbal expressions of the characters rather than the physical mechanics or punitive aspects of the bullying.
